quote: If you're logged in, I can help you locate the usage.
stewart_read: Rep offers to talk the customer through the portal live rather than defer or pivot to verbal readback, extending an already-long technical struggle.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be strategically staying patient to avoid losing the lead by hanging up mid-struggle — but the schema explicitly calls for a 2-minute pivot budget, which is blown well past here.
coaching_implication: Should have pivoted to 'just read me the monthly kWh numbers off the bill' within 2 minutes per the elderly_low_tech_protocol; instead the struggle ran roughly 17 minutes.

quote: If I send you a text, could you actually send me a photo of what you're looking at, like a screenshot?
stewart_read: A reasonable attempted pivot to photo/text, but it still requires the customer to correctly navigate to the right screen first — doesn't solve the underlying navigation confusion.
coaching_implication: A true pivot would ask for a verbal read of the 12-month kWh bars rather than another screenshot dependent on correct navigation.

quote: that one that you're showing me is actually going off the costs instead of the usage
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the cost/usage confusion; rep corrects but the underlying navigation problem recurs two more times afterward.
coaching_implication: Multi-touch pattern — see multi_touch_patterns entry; rep should have named the exact screen element (bar graph, top-left) on the first correction instead of the third.

quote: And then there's a little bar graph in the top left corner.
stewart_read: This precise instruction is what finally resolves the multi-touch confusion, but it came 17 minutes into the call instead of on the first ask.
coaching_implication: Front-load the exact visual location descriptor at the first bill-usage request to save the bulk of this call's runtime.

quote: So that's actually what my specialist would come over to show you guys.
stewart_read: Rep correctly deflects a pricing question to the specialist instead of answering it herself — good scope discipline.
coaching_implication: This is the one clean positive move in the call; reinforce as the model for handling 'what does it cost' questions.

quote: he has some other company too. They came you know, they they got in contact with me too.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a competing company already contacted him; rep acknowledges but doesn't probe which company or what was offered.
coaching_implication: Should have asked 'which company, and what did they quote you?' to surface competitive intel and pre-empt price objections at the closer's meeting.

quote: they told me, you know, another company told me that I I'm, you know, the the panelists are free, and they don't have to pay anything
stewart_read: Customer states a cost/value confusion pulled from a competitor's pitch; rep validates without flipping it back to the customer's own bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically avoiding an argument over a competitor's claim to keep the tone calm — but no flip was attempted at all, so this reads as a missed opportunity rather than a deliberate hold.
coaching_implication: Could have flipped with something like referencing his own $224 bill jump as the real cost of staying with ComEd instead of letting the 'free panels' claim sit unchallenged.
